assessment: Member 125 reports a dribbling item by visit and genetic associations, with inconsistent denominators across captions and methods. Member 162 reports a salivation difference by motor subtype without item magnitude. No food intervention in either.
The PKAN validation separates a salivation item from swallowing and food handling. It tests instrument responses in a different underlying condition without an intervention.
One original interview account discusses avoiding public settings because of drooling and food spills. The report has no assigned food or comparative symptom rating.

Original Table 2 gives low stimulated flow in 26/30 Parkinson participants and 13/26 eligible controls, while reported dryness was excluded at control recruitment. No isolated drooling estimate and no fig exposure.
The original survey abstract gives distinct self-reported drooling, oral dryness and dysphagia outcomes. No raw-fig intake or measured direction. Original result tables are open.

Among 75 diary participants, the abstract separately describes drooling, dysphagia and xerostomia. Food intake is associated with the dry-mouth outcome. No ingredient-specific drooling results are established.
The prospective registry records hourly symptom and activity logs for 75 adults. It directly links the Barbe diary report and adds no independent sample or ingredient comparison.
The primary abstract reports prior UPDRS salivation ratings and associations with motor subtype among 586 Parkinson patients. No reported raw-fig exposure and the original tables remain open.
The later Wenzhou report has 101 participants and a gastrointestinal domain result. It has no separately published salivation outcome. Participant overlap with the 2019 member remains open.
